concept.title: Choose a starter preset before detailed policy editing
concept.shortdesc: Starter presets seed a BPM profile for common environments before you review, validate, and adjust individual Firefox policies.

section.title: Purpose
section.p: A starter preset is a BPM baseline, not a finished deployment recommendation. Use it to create an initial policy set, then inspect every changed value in Guided editor, All settings, or JSON editor before export.

section.title: Basic corporate
section.p: Choose the corporate preset when the profile should favor managed updates, telemetry reduction, account and Pocket restrictions, enterprise roots, system proxy, a locked intranet homepage, controlled downloads, and blocked default extension installation.

section.title: Classroom kiosk
section.p: Choose the classroom or kiosk preset when the browser starts from a locked school page, uses constrained browsing behavior, limits private browsing and internal pages, and can force a reviewed classroom extension while keeping other extensions blocked.

section.title: Protected station
section.p: Choose the protected-station preset for hardened workstations or SOC-style environments that need stricter proxy, DNS, certificate, permission, private browsing, extension, and preference controls. Review every network and certificate value before export because environment-specific placeholders must be replaced.

section.title: After selection
section.p: After applying a preset, validate the selected Firefox channel, inspect source tracing, remove unwanted values, and export only a reviewed policies.json. A CIS layer can be added separately when the profile needs a documented security baseline.
